# Task mapping

Every correspondence between the tasks in the Catalog and the paradigm classes of
[CogPO](http://www.cogpo.org/), the Cognitive Paradigm Ontology, in both directions,
the counterpart of the Atlas [task mapping](../atlas/task_mapping.md) page: a
summary of each direction by match type, then the full row tables. The
[CogPO mapping method](../methods/cogpo_mapping_method.md) page explains what the match
types mean and how each row was decided, and [The Catalog vs CogPO](the_catalog_vs_cogpo.md)
says what the correspondence adds up to.

The source of record is `data/mappings/`, not this page. A CogPO class name links to
its page on the CogPO wiki, the only place the class can be read online; the wiki is
reachable over plain http only, because its certificate is invalid. The two Oddball
subclasses have no wiki page and are not linked.


The kind assigned to each unmatched class is a hand-checked judgement, not a rule: with
86 classes, every one was read against its definition. The first group is the one that
matters for the Catalog, since each entry is a task it could list.

```{include} ../_generated/cogpo_paradigm_unmatched.md
```

## Reading the two directions together

The directions answer different questions. The Catalog-to-CogPO table asks whether CogPO
has a class for a given task; the CogPO-to-Catalog table asks, for each CogPO class,
whether the Catalog covers it. A CogPO class that is a broad family (Reward Task,
Encoding, Visual Attention) can therefore be `related` to one Catalog task in the second
table while eight tasks point at it as `related` in the first. Both statements are true:
the class covers them all and is none of them.
